haiku-low.q1: The connection comes back, the app comes to the foreground, or 60 seconds pass while online.
haiku-low.q2: The upload happens first, then the download.
haiku-low.q3: The server detects it by comparing the change's base version with the note's current version; a mismatch is a conflict.
haiku-low.q4: The first phone's edit is stored as version 2. The second phone's body is saved as a new note titled the original title plus " (conflict)".
haiku-low.q5: One change: the newest full body, keeping the original base version and change ID.
haiku-low.q6: Each change has a unique change ID. The server checks processed change IDs first and returns the saved result without applying it again.
haiku-low.q7: On the phone, as its cursor (last applied sequence number). It is updated in the same local write that saves the applied entries.
haiku-low.q8: Nothing from that download is saved, the cursor does not move, and the next sync asks again from the same cursor.
haiku-low.q9: The server answers conflict on upload, and the phone removes the change. It then downloads the winning version of the original note.
haiku-low.q10: Once the server answers accepted or conflict to its upload.
haiku-low.q12: The sent change is never edited. The new edit becomes a later, separate change in the outbox.

sonnet.q1: The connection coming back, the app coming to the foreground, or 60 seconds passing while online.
sonnet.q3: The server. It compares the change's base version to the note's current version; if they are not equal, it is a conflict.
sonnet.q4: The first phone's change is saved as version 2 of the note and logged. The second phone's body is saved as a new note titled with the original title plus " (conflict)" and logged. Both phones end up with version 2 and the conflict copy.
sonnet.q5: One change. Edits to the same note replace the unsent change's body, keeping its original base version and change ID, so it sends a single change with the latest full body.
sonnet.q6: Each change has a unique change ID, and the server records processed change IDs. If a change ID is already processed, the server returns the saved result and applies nothing.
sonnet.q7: The phone stores a cursor (its last applied sequence number). It is updated in the same single local write that saves the new entries, so it moves only past applied entries.
sonnet.q8: Nothing was saved and the cursor did not move, so the next sync asks again from the same cursor. No entry is skipped or missed.
sonnet.q9: The server reports a conflict for the change, saying the body is kept as a copy. The phone then downloads the log entries, including the conflict copy and the winning version of the original note, and applies them.
sonnet.q10: When the server answers accepted or conflict. It stays in the outbox if the upload or answer is lost.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED. The document lists it as an open question: a sent change is never edited and a later edit creates a new change, but which base version the new edit gets is not specified.
